items.title: David Torkanowsky interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, September 26, 2019
items.q: one of my best courses at Berklee was Herb Pomeroy’s Line Writing class

ctx.x: Even Ellington, his writing was more like that. He had all those lines going on.

Correct. Matter of fact one of my best courses at Berklee was Herb Pomeroy’s Line Writing class. And it’s like you started with this note and you ended with this note and you’re whole thing was to write an interesting melody. Now the bass, or the next voice, just start at this point, end at this point, and write an interesting melody. And then look, I mean the strength of the melody is so strong that the harmony makes itself. It’s like Nicholas Payton can play, we were playing a D minor construct, D minor…
Wow. You hung out with Danny Barker and Erroll Garner?
